clue.text: Hussy's unclothed with detective after day in Riviera location

indicators.note: the detective comes after the day, so the day's letters go first

parts.note: MON is the short form of Monday
TEC is short for detective

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters of the word are removed

parts.note: a hussy is a harlot; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A scandalous woman strips off beside a private eye on a day out on the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unclothed' strips the outer letters, first and last, from the word for a hussy; 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo is the glamorous resort in Monaco on the Mediterranean coast known as the Riviera.

clue.text: Shabby Shakespearean fairy employed by school broadcast

parts.note: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so we want a word sounding like the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A tatty production of a Shakespeare play put on by a school, with a fairy in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON, the English boarding school, said aloud gives EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes riddled with holes from moth larvae look worn and shabby, hence the figurative sense.

clue.text: Woman to take home incredibly neat clothes

indicators.note: as a verb, the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece like a garment
used in the sense of wildly or unbelievably, telling us the word neat is rearranged

parts.note: take-home pay is net pay

explanation.surface: Someone's going to bring home some wonderfully tidy clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like garments but is a verb: the rearranged letters wrap around the take-home pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a female given name, so any woman could bear it.

clue.text: Response when Conservative rises in the world

indicators.note: in a down clue, a letter that rises moves higher up the column, so earlier in the word

parts.note: a reaction is a response

explanation.surface: A political commentator noting how people react when the Tories gain ground globally.
explanation.walkthrough: In REACTION the C climbs to the top of the down entry, giving CREATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation is everything that exists, the whole universe or world as made.

clue.text: Resort to accommodate student starting in some further education?

indicators.note: to house or take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to have recourse to something is to resort to it
a fresher is a student in their first term at university

explanation.surface: A holiday spot laying on rooms for a new student taking an adult-education class.
explanation.walkthrough: A fresher is the British word for a first-year university student.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course updates existing skills, a kind of continuing or further training; the question mark flags the loose example.

clue.text: Where democracy initially denied, draws lots

indicators.note: refused, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to doodle is to draw idly

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the word supplying its first letter

explanation.surface: In a state without democracy, the ballot is replaced by drawing lots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws lots' looks like a single phrase, but 'draws' is the wordplay and 'lots' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is an informal word for a great quantity, just as lots is.

clue.text: Impact one expects to have?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knock or collision
second meaning: an expectant mother's swollen belly; 'one expects' plays on expecting a baby

explanation.walkthrough: 'Expects' reads as merely anticipating, but here it means being pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is both a collision and the colloquial term for the visible pregnancy belly.

clue.text: With two parties involved, bare it all when dancing

indicators.note: letters moving about as if on a dance floor, so the words bare it all are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky note about stripping off on the dance floor when there are two parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral describes an agreement or talks between two sides, such as two nations.

clue.text: Period said to be this writer's speciality — nothing in that

indicators.note: the zero goes inside what has just been built
the phrase is heard, so we spell what it sounds like

parts.note: the writer's own speciality is 'my scene', my particular field
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An author claiming an expertise, then admitting there is nothing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My scene' said aloud is MI-CENE; O placed inside gives MI-O-CENE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miocene is a geological epoch, a time period roughly 23 to 5 million years ago.

clue.text: As one might be, having confused note with four others?

definitions.text: As one might be, having confused note with four others?

indicators.note: jumbled up, so the letters of note are rearranged

parts.note: D, E, A and F are four further musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps singing the wrong note might well be described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTE rearranged gives TONE, followed by four other notes of the scale, D, E, A, F; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person unable to tell pitches apart would muddle one musical note with others.

clue.text: Unstructured mass survey needs sending back to party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: returning it, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a poll is a survey of opinion

explanation.surface: An opinion survey being returned to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, but here it is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump or blob of something soft, such as cream.

clue.text: Comes in, displacing monarch, to find wooden characters

indicators.note: pushing out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: enters means comes in
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the monarch

explanation.surface: Someone enters, ousting a king, and finds puppets on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden characters' suggests stiff actors or puppets; it means tree beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ents are the tree-like giants in Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, literally made of wood.

clue.text: Fabulous group fashionably late appearing in ancient city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters show up inside the city

parts.note: Thebes was a city of ancient Greece and also of Egypt

indicators.note: arriving fashionably late, the letters of late are rearranged in style

explanation.surface: A legendary band turns up fashionably late to play in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' points to the band's nickname, the Fab Four, rather than to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were nicknamed the Fab Four, so a fabulous band in both senses.

clue.text: Mystical system Henry introduced to eccentric Soho type

indicators.note: brought into, so the letter is placed inside
odd or off-centre, so the letters of Soho type are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry is introduced to a quirky London Soho character who practises mysticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a bohemian district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a philosophical movement claiming mystical insight into the divine.

clue.text: Building old and as you see unfinished

parts.note: thou is the old word for you

indicators.note: not completed, so the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: the word see itself

explanation.surface: Showing someone an old, half-built building.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a kiln building for drying hops, common in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast house is a farm building with a distinctive conical roof, used for drying hops.

clue.text: Snake applying pressure to indigenous North Americans

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A snake putting the squeeze on Native Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' reads as a noun, but it is a verb meaning to move sinuously.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake and to creep both describe moving slowly and stealthily along.

clue.text: Class in gym excited, enthralled by outstanding teacher

parts.note: PE, physical education, is a class held in the gym

indicators.note: held captive by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a debt that is outstanding is due
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: Pupils in a gym lesson are thrilled by a brilliant teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as excellent; here it means owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster or instructor, often a pedantic one.

clue.text: Not feeling pressure in extremely close finish

parts.note: a numb limb is dead, without feeling
heat means pressure, as in the heat is on

explanation.surface: An athlete numb to the pressure in a photo finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race where competitors cross the line together, a tie.

clue.text: Strangler's device police informer carries round

indicators.note: holds within, so the round letter goes inside

parts.note: nose is slang for a police informer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A grass carrying a garrotte on his rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose' is British slang for someone who tips off the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope that tightens to strangle, as used by a hangman.

clue.text: Zero put on tax? One at work gives sustained applause

indicators.note: in a down entry, the zero is placed on top of the tax

parts.note: O looks like zero
VAT is value added tax
I is the Roman numeral one
on means working, as in on duty

explanation.surface: Bewilderment at a zero-rated tax that earns cheering at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the British sales tax, value added tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is prolonged enthusiastic applause from an audience.

clue.text: Youth alive to climate crisis crossing northern country

parts.note: green describes someone environmentally aware

indicators.note: the letter cuts across the middle of the word

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young climate activist sailing to a northern land.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenland is a vast Arctic island territory, an autonomous country within the Danish realm.

clue.text: Abrasive former student one's interrupted

indicators.note: broken into, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an alumna is a female graduate
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A prickly ex-student cut off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive' reads as a personality; it is the noun, a grinding material.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumina, aluminium oxide, is used as a grinding and polishing material.

clue.text: Cheeses spoken of for picnic

indicators.note: talked about, so it is the sound that matters, not the spelling

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Cheeses mentioned as food for an outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picnic' looks like a meal but means something easy, as in 'no picnic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze, like a picnic, is informal for an easy task.

clue.text: Being old man, large ruffian should contain reduced crowd

indicators.note: is to hold, so the shortened piece goes inside

parts.note: fat means large
hood is short for hoodlum, a ruffian

indicators.note: cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a herd is a crowd

explanation.surface: A burly thug is supposed to keep back a smaller crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatherhood is the state of being a father, the old man of a family.

clue.text: Small cake presented with good sweetener

parts.note: a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A cake served with something sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' looks culinary but means a bribe; 'bung' is British slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a bribe, an inducement or sweetener paid on the side.

clue.text: I'd turned medieval guitar's tone down

indicators.note: turned around, so read backwards

parts.note: the lute is a medieval stringed instrument like a guitar; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A musician lowering the tone of an old lute.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute is to weaken or soften something, making it less intense.

clue.text: Bothering to swallow what's in best wine

indicators.note: to take in, so the inner letters go inside

parts.note: riling means annoying, bothering

indicators.note: the letters inside, all but the first and last

explanation.surface: Irritated at having to drink a fine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape variety and the wine made from it, from Germany and Alsace.

clue.text: Cry out in sorrow when displacing back joint

indicators.note: the back letter of the word is moved to another position

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief

explanation.surface: Wailing in pain when a back joint is dislocated.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEN's final N moves forward to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Reader worried by Burke or Hare finally choosing body

indicators.note: points to the final letter

parts.note: the Edinburgh body-snatchers Burke and Hare; either name ends in the same letter
a lector reads lessons in church
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A reader is troubled that Burke or Hare is picking out a body.
explanation.walkthrough: Burke and Hare were 1820s murderers who sold corpses for dissection, so 'body' has a grim surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An electorate is the body of voters who choose representatives in an election.
